facts.summary: Indiana's minimum wage is $7.25 per hour, adopting the federal rate by reference; it has not increased since 2009.
facts.notes: Same as federal $7.25. Indiana has no scheduled increase. Tipped cash wage is $2.13 with tip credit.

facts.summary: Indiana requires overtime at 1.5x after 40 hours in a workweek and has no daily-overtime rule or higher salary floor than federal law.
facts.notes: State Minimum Wage Law mirrors federal FLSA overtime; most employers are covered by FLSA directly. Exemptions are listed at Ind. Code 22-2-2-3.

facts.summary: Indiana's civil rights law covers race, color, religion, sex, disability, national origin, plus ancestry and veteran status (the latter in employment).
facts.notes: Ancestry and veteran status are additions beyond the core federal set. Age is handled by a separate chapter (Ind. Code 22-9-2).

facts.summary: The Indiana Civil Rights Law covers employers with six or more employees, lower than the federal 15-employee threshold.
facts.sourceAgency: Indiana General Assembly / Indiana Civil Rights Commission
facts.notes: Employers with 6-14 employees fall under state (ICRC) jurisdiction but below the federal 15-employee Title VII/ADA threshold. Verify subsection letter against current statute text; the six-employee figure is set in the 'employer' definition of Ind. Code 22-9-1-3.

facts.summary: Indiana's separate Age Discrimination Act protects workers aged 40-74 at employers with one or more employees, filling the gap below the federal ADEA (20+ employees).
facts.notes: Applies only to employers NOT subject to the federal ADEA, so it primarily covers small employers. Protects persons who have attained age 40 but not 75.

facts.summary: A discrimination complaint must be filed with the Indiana Civil Rights Commission within 180 days of the alleged discriminatory act.
facts.notes: State deadline is 180 days, shorter than the EEOC's 300-day deferral-state deadline for federal charges. Verify subsection letter against statute text.

facts.summary: Final wages (whether the employee quits or is discharged) are due on or before the next regularly scheduled payday.
facts.notes: Indiana has no requirement for immediate final pay upon discharge; regular payday timing applies. Regular pay must occur at least semi-monthly/biweekly. sourceUrl updated 2026-08-25: the prior Indiana DOL FAQ page (secure.in.gov/dol/wage-and-hour/wage-and-hour-faqs/, and its www.in.gov mirror) returned 404 on verification, so this now cites the current Indiana Code Title 22 portal (the primary statutory source for Ind. Code 22-2-5-1 and 22-2-9-2) instead; re-confirm if IDOL republishes a live FAQ page.

facts.value: file with Indiana DOL; unpaid-wage civil actions generally within 2 years
facts.summary: Unpaid-wage claims are filed with the Indiana Department of Labor under the Wage Claims (former employees) and Wage Payment (current/voluntarily separated) statutes.
facts.notes: The DOL page does not state a filing deadline; the general 2-year civil statute of limitations for wage actions (Ind. Code 34-11-2-1) is commonly applied but was not confirmed on an official DOL page. Verify the 2-year figure before publishing.

facts.summary: Indiana law protects employees who report a violation of federal, state, or local law or misuse of public resources from retaliation; violation is a Class A infraction.
facts.notes: Strongest protections apply to employees of private employers under public contract and to public employees; report to the employer or an appropriate government official is required.
